dosing_regimen.source_excerpt: protocolSection.armsInterventionsModule.interventions and armGroups: "Participants will receive a weight-based dose of guselkumab subcutaneously." "Part 1 Group 1: Guselkumab" "Part 1 Group 2: Placebo for Guselkumab" "Part 1 Group 3: Etanercept" "Part 2: Guselkumab" "Participants will receive a weight-based dose of placebo for guselkumab subcutaneously." "Part 1 Group 1: Guselkumab" "Part 1 Group 2: Placebo for Guselkumab" "Etanercept" "Participants will receive a weight-based dose of etanercept (up to 50 mg) subcutaneously." "Part 1 Group 3: Etanercept" "Participants in Part 1a (age greater than or equal to (\>=) 12 - less than (\<) 18 years) will receive a weight-based dose of guselkumab subcutaneously (SC) at Weeks 0, 4, and 12." "Participants who are PASI 90 responders at Week 16 will not receive any additional doses of guselkumab until they lose \>=50% of their Week 16 PASI response, then they receive 1 dose guselkumab, followed by a dose 4 weeks later, and every 8 weeks (q8w) thereafter through Week 52." "Participants in Part 1a (age \>= 12 - \<18 years) will receive placebo for guselkumab administered SC at Weeks 0, 4, and 12." "Participants who are PASI 90 non-responders at Week 16 will receive a weight-based guselkumab dose at Weeks 16 and 20, followed by q8w dosing thereafter through Week 52." "Participants in Part 1a (age \>= 12 - \<18 years) will receive weight-based etanercept dose up to 50 milligram SC weekly through Week 15." "Participants who elect to continue in the study will receive a weight-based guselkumab dose at Weeks 20 and 24, followed by q8w dosing thereafter through Week 48." "Participants will receive a weight-based dose of open-label guselkumab SC at Weeks 0, 4 and q8w thereafter through Week 52." "Part 1 Group 3: Etanercept" -- Includes all three CT.gov interventions. Guselkumab and placebo dosing varies by study part and post-Week-16 response; guselkumab has a Week-0/4/12 initial regimen in Part 1 and a separate Part 2 regimen. Etanercept is weight-based (0.8 mg/kg below 63 kg or 50 mg at or above 63 kg) and is given weekly through Week 15. The schema cannot encode these weight bands or response-dependent dose sequences as a single dose, frequency, or continuous dosing period, so those fields remain null or empty. Intervention descriptions are copied verbatim from CT.gov. The intervention-arm links are the registry's armGroupLabels and include crossover/intervention assignments.

severity_criteria.source_excerpt: Clinical Studies, section 14.1, pediatric Trial PsO5 eligibility description: "Pediatric Subjects with Moderate-to-Severe Plaque Psoriasis Trial PsO5 One multicenter, randomized, placebo and active biological comparator-controlled trial (PsO5 [NCT03451851]) enrolled 120 subjects 6 years to 17 years of age with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who were candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy and inadequately controlled by phototherapy and/or topical therapies." "Subjects had an IGA score of ≥3 (" "moderate" ") on a 5-point scale of overall disease severity, a PASI ≥12, and a minimum affected BSA of ≥10%, and at least one of the following: 1) very thick lesions, 2) clinically relevant facial, genital, or hand/foot involvement, 3) PASI ≥20, 4) BSA >20%, or 5) IGA=4 (" "severe" ")." -- The label states these thresholds together and additionally requires at least one of: very thick lesions; clinically relevant facial, genital, or hand/foot involvement; PASI >=20; BSA >20%; or IGA=4. The scale thresholds above are the quantitative criteria representable as ScoreCriterion rows.

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: 5.4.1 US-FDA specific Multiplicity Adjustment for Testing Procedures: "Multiplicity Adjustment for Testing Procedures" "The US-FDA specific co-primary endpoints are:" " The proportion of subjects who achieve an IGA score of cleared (0) or minimal (1) at Week 16" " The proportion of subjects who achieve a PASI 90 response at Week 16" "Both of the US-FDA specific co-primary endpoint analyses will be compared between the" "guselkumab treatment group and the placebo group and tested at a 2-sided α-level of 0.05." "In addition, the following US-FDA specific major secondary endpoints will be compared between" "the guselkumab group and the placebo group:" " The proportion of subjects who achieve a PASI 75 response at Week 16." " The proportion of subjects who achieve an IGA score of cleared (0) at Week 16." " The proportion of subjects who achieve a PASI 100 response at Week 16." " The change from baseline in CDLQI at Week 16" "In order to control the overall Type 1 error rate, the US-FDA specific co-primary analyses and" "major secondary analyses will be tested in a fixed sequence as ordered above." "of the major secondary endpoints will be performed only if both primary analyses are significant" "and will be performed in the fixed sequence testing approach, as specified above." "In Part 1 of the study, participants with a PASI score increase of ≥50% from their baseline PASI" "score at Week 8 or Week 12 will be allowed to use a topical steroid as rescue treatment up until" "Week 16, with the exception of ultra-high potency topical steroids (eg, clobetasol propionate," "halobetasol propionate) which are not allowed at any time." "It is recommended that participants use" "no more than 60 grams of topical steroids per week." "Participants must" "discontinue the use of rescue topical steroids by Week 20." "Subjects who use a low to high potency topical steroid starting at Week 8 or Week 12 as a result" "of being eligible for rescue treatment will be considered as nonresponders for binary endpoints" "and zero (no change from baseline) will be assigned to continuous outcomes from that point" "onward through Week 16." -- The SAP's US-FDA specific testing plan treats IGA 0/1 and PASI 90 at Week 16 as co-primary, then tests PASI 75, IGA 0, PASI 100, and CDLQI in the stated fixed sequence at two-sided alpha 0.05 to control overall Type I error. The global plan differs (PASI 75 rather than PASI 90 is co-primary); this field represents the US-FDA-specific plan. Rescue-eligible topical-steroid use is treated as nonresponse for binary endpoints through Week 16. The SAP explicitly says the sequence controls overall Type I error; this supports familywise_error_controlled=true and gatekeeping_structure=true. The rescue rule explicitly says eligible topical-steroid use counts as nonresponse for binary endpoints.

study_schedule.source_excerpt: Protocol Amendment 5 §§1.1–1.3 and 4.2; synopsis/periods and Schedule of Activities text: "A long-term extension (LTE) of the study will be initiated at Week 52." "Group I: Weight-based guselkumab dose CCI SC at Weeks 0, 4, and 12." "Group II: Weight-based placebo for guselkumab dose administered SC at Weeks 0, 4, and 12." "Group III: Weight-based etanercept dose up to 50 mg SC weekly through Week 15." "Group III: Participants randomized to etanercept who elect to continue in the study will receive a" "Participants randomized to etanercept will receive an etanercept dose weekly from Week 0 through Week 15." "Participants randomized to etanercept will then have the option to initiate a weight-based guselkumab dose regimen with injections at Week 20 and 24 followed by" "extension of the study will receive guselkumab at Week 52 followed by q8w administration beginning at Week 60 in the long-term extension." "All participants who complete either Part 1 or Part 2 of the main study through Week 52 will be" "The end of the main study is defined as the timepoint when the last participant completes the" "The end of the complete study is defined as the timepoint when the last participant" "The screening phase of up to 10 weeks will allow for sufficient time to perform screening study" "regimen of guselkumab will be evaluated in pediatric participants during a 16-week randomized," "retreatment or initiation of treatment with guselkumab through Week 52." "From Week 16 through Week 52:" "to the study site every 8 weeks for safety and efficacy assessments in addition to study intervention" "the proportion of participants achieving a Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) 75 response at Week 16." "evaluations for at least 12 weeks following the last dose of study intervention (see Section 7.1) and complete all procedures and evaluations listed under the Study" "asked to return for a study termination visit 12 weeks after their last administration of study intervention." "1.3." "Schedule of Activities (SoA)..........................................................................................................." "1.3.1." "Screening Through Week 52 –Part 1a and 1b.........................................................................." "1.3.2." "Screening Through Week 52 –Part 2 ........................................................................................" "1.3.3." "Long-term Extension Phase (Week 60 Through Study Completion/Termination) ....................." -- The protocol defines a 16-week randomized controlled Part 1 followed by withdrawal/retreatment or treatment through Week 52; Part 2 is open-label through Week 52. The LTE begins at Week 52, with continued q8w guselkumab and site assessments every 8 weeks. Week 52 is the end of the main study, not the end of treatment for participants continuing into the LTE, so end_of_treatment_week is null. The protocol describes screening as up to approximately 10 weeks, which cannot be faithfully expressed in screening_days. The cited Protocol Amendment 5 contains a dedicated Schedule of Activities with separate Part 1, Part 2, and LTE schedules (Section 1.3, pages 14–21), so full_visit_table_available is true; the plain-text extraction does not reproduce the table grid. it does not establish a fixed LTE end or whole-study duration. A screening phase of up to approximately 10 weeks before Week 0 is stated but not converted into days. Participants who discontinue intervention may have at least 12 weeks of continued protocol procedures after their last dose; participants who do not enter the LTE are asked to return 12 weeks after their last administration, so this follow-up timing is relative to an individual last dose and is not assigned an absolute trial week.

value.applies_to_period: Part 1; topical rescue permitted after qualifying PASI worsening at Week 8 or Week 12 and through Week 16
value.rationale: Participants with a PASI score increase of at least 50% from baseline at Week 8 or Week 12 may use topical-steroid rescue until Week 16; ultra-high-potency topical steroids are excluded, use is limited to a recommended maximum of 60 g/week and lowest possible potency/frequency, and rescue steroids must stop by Week 20 (not initiated at or after Week 16). The closed ScoreCriterion metrics cannot represent an increase in score from baseline, so trigger_rules is empty and the source threshold is preserved here. Rescue-eligible topical-steroid use counts as nonresponse for binary endpoints through Week 16.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: 5.1.3.4 Rescue Treatment and 5.1.3.5 Rescue Treatment Rules: "Rescue Treatment" "In Part 1 of the study, participants with a PASI score increase of ≥50% from their baseline PASI" "score at Week 8 or Week 12 will be allowed to use a topical steroid as rescue treatment up until" "Week 16, with the exception of ultra-high potency topical steroids (eg, clobetasol propionate," "halobetasol propionate) which are not allowed at any time." "It is recommended that participants use" "no more than 60 grams of topical steroids per week." "In addition, participants should be managed" "using the lowest possible potency and frequency of rescue topical steroid." "Participants must" "discontinue the use of rescue topical steroids by Week 20." "Rescue Treatment Rules" "Subjects who use a low to high potency topical steroid starting at Week 8 or Week 12 as a result" "of being eligible for rescue treatment will be considered as nonresponders for binary endpoints" "and zero (no change from baseline) will be assigned to continuous outcomes from that point" "onward through Week 16." -- The source's threshold is worsening (an increase of PASI score from baseline), which cannot be truthfully mapped to a closed ScoreCriterion metric. The rationale carries its exact timing and exception details. The SAP says this rescue handling applies to Part 1. The SAP explicitly says qualifying participants will be allowed to use topical-steroid rescue and explicitly assigns nonresponder status for binary endpoints.

published_results.source_excerpt: Clinical Studies, section 14.1, Table 7 efficacy results at Week 16 in Trial PsO5: "Pediatric Subjects with Moderate-to-Severe Plaque Psoriasis Trial PsO5 One multicenter, randomized, placebo and active biological comparator-controlled trial (PsO5 [NCT03451851]) enrolled 120 subjects 6 years to 17 years of age with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who were candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy and inadequately controlled by phototherapy and/or topical therapies." "In trial PsO5, 92 subjects were randomized to receive subcutaneous injection of either TREMFYA (N=41) or placebo (N=25) at Weeks 0, 4, and 12 or an active biological comparator (N=26)." "Clinical Response Table 7 presents the efficacy results at Week 16 in trial PsO5." "Table 7: Efficacy Results at Week 16 in Pediatric Subjects 6 Years of Age and Older with Moderate-to-Severe Plaque Psoriasis in Trial PsO5 (NRI NRI = Non-Responder Imputation ) Endpoint Trial PsO5 Placebo (N=25) n (%) TREMFYA (N=41) n (%) Treatment Difference (95% CI) IGA response of 0/1 Co-primary endpoint , IGA response of 0 (" "cleared" ") or 1 (" "minimal" ") 4 (16) 27 (66) 50 (26, 69) IGA response of 0 (cleared) 1 (4) 16 (39) 35 (11, 57) PASI 75 response 5 (20) 31 (76) 56 (32, 74) PASI 90 response 4 (16) 23 (56) 40 (16, 61) PASI 100 response 0 14 (34) 34 (10, 56) 14.2 Clinical Studies in Adults with Active Psoriatic Arthritis The safety and efficacy of TREMFYA were assessed in 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (PsA1 [NCT03162796], PsA2 [NCT03158285], and PsA3 [NCT04882098]) in adult subjects with active psoriatic arthritis (PsA) (≥3 swollen joints, ≥3 tender joints, and a C-reactive protein (CRP) level of ≥0.3 mg/dL in PsA1 and PsA3 and ≥5 swollen joints, ≥5 tender joints, and a CRP level of ≥0.6 mg/dL in PsA2) who had inadequate response to standard therapies (e.g., conventional DMARDs [cDMARDs]), apremilast, or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDs])." -- Table 7 gives Week 16 n (%) by Placebo (N=25) and TREMFYA (N=41) for the controlled PsO5 trial. FDA label section 14.1 explicitly identifies PsO5 as NCT03451851. Row values and percentages are copied as printed. The label's US-FDA co-primary narrative names IGA 0/1 and PASI 90; the posted protocol/registry global primary endpoint list names IGA 0/1 and PASI 75. Each Table 7 result is joined only to an exact Week 16 endpoint key from endpoint_keys.json; the table's treatment-difference confidence intervals are not arm-specific and are omitted. rate_is_derived=false because the label prints n (%) directly for each percentage row. Secondary endpoint position 2 is the exact canonical endpoint_keys.json lookup for the IGA-cleared Week 16 outcome, not a clinical count.
